issues.legal_issue: When a contract fixes a date for performance, the limitation period for a specific-performance claim begins on that date even if time is not of the essence.
material_facts: The parties’ sale agreement fixed May 28, 1989, as the date for performance.
The purchasers argued that time was not of the essence and that there was an oral agreement to perform after the seller obtained required permissions.
The application to add a specific-performance claim was filed on November 5, 1992.
issues.conclusion: Because the agreement fixed a date for performance, limitation began to run from that date under the first part of Article 54; whether time was of the essence was not material to that computation. The specific-performance claim therefore had to be brought within three years of the fixed date, absent an agreed extension.
issues.legal_principle: Section 3 and the first part of Article 54 of the Limitation Act, 1963, provide that a specific-performance claim must be brought within three years from the date fixed for performance. Whether time is of the essence does not affect that rule. Chand Rani (dead) by LRs. v. Kamal Rani (dead) by LRs. explains the distinction between time being of the essence and the limitation period running from a fixed date; K. Raheja Construction Ltd. v. Alliances Ministries and Tarlok Singh v. Vijay Kumar Sabharwal apply the fixed-date rule. Ramzan v. Hussaini explains that a date may be fixed by reference to an event that makes it ascertainable.

rule.if: specific_performance_limitation_claim and performance_date_fixed and not performance_deadline_extended

predicates.specific_performance_limitation_claim: The proceeding seeks specific performance of a contract.
predicates.performance_date_fixed: The parties fixed a date for performance, either directly or by reference to an event that makes the date ascertainable.
predicates.performance_deadline_extended: The parties agreed to extend the fixed performance deadline.

issues.definition: When a specific-performance claim concerns a contract with a fixed performance date and the parties have not extended that deadline, the limitation period runs from the fixed date.

issues.legal_issue: An amendment adding a specific-performance claim cannot be allowed when it is sought after the limitation period has expired, even if the original suit sought a different form of relief.
material_facts: The purchasers initially sued for a mandatory injunction directing the seller to comply with requirements in the agreement.
They later applied to amend the plaint to seek specific performance.
The agreement fixed May 28, 1989, as the performance date, and the amendment application was filed on November 5, 1992.
The trial court rejected the amendment, and the High Court affirmed that decision.
issues.conclusion: The amendment was sought after the specific-performance claim had become barred by limitation and was properly refused. The appeal was dismissed, subject to the seller’s undertaking to refund the amount paid with interest as stipulated in the contract.
issues.legal_principle: Under Article 54 of the Limitation Act, 1963, a specific-performance claim based on a fixed performance date must be brought within three years from that date. A suit for mandatory injunction is different from a suit for specific performance, and adding the latter by amendment after its limitation period has expired cannot cure the bar. Order VI, Rule 17 of the Code of Civil Procedure governs amendment of pleadings. K. Raheja Construction Ltd. v. Alliances Ministries and Tarlok Singh v. Vijay Kumar Sabharwal support refusing an amendment that introduces a time-barred specific-performance claim.

predicates.specific_performance_claim_added_by_amen: A party seeks to add a claim for specific performance by amending a pleading.
predicates.performance_date_fixed: The parties fixed a date for performance, either directly or by reference to an event that makes the date ascertainable.
predicates.amendment_after_limitation_period: The amendment is sought after the limitation period for the specific-performance claim has expired.

issues.definition: If a party seeks to add specific performance by amendment after the limitation period has expired from a fixed performance date, the amendment is barred.
